final_message:
**Status:** Reproduced (also reproduces on 5.7.2; passes on 5.6.3)

**Expected:** `Test` displays as `{ prop1: "hello"; }`, as on 5.6.3.

**Actual:** On this checkout (5.8.0-dev, 6b1ea96b9) the checker prints `Test` as `{ prop1: Wrapper<"hello">; }`. Same on 5.7.2. No diagnostics are reported.

**Trigger:** The code from the report, with the assertion inline in the `objWrapper({ prop1: stringWrapper() as Wrapper<"hello"> })` call. Putting the assertion on its own line (`const strWrapper = ... as Wrapper<"hello">`) prints `{ prop1: "hello"; }`. `repro/run.js` runs this as a control.

**Run:** `node repro/run.js` (exits 1 and prints `BUG` when it reproduces). To compare against another build, pass its typescript.js path as an argument. I installed 5.6.3 and 5.7.2 under /tmp for that. Both are scratch, not part of the patch.

**Observations that may help the investigation:**
- The wrong text is a printing problem, not a type-resolution one. `getPropertiesOfType(Test)` returns `prop1: "hello"` on 5.7.2 and on this checkout. `Test` is assignable to `{ prop1: "hello" }` and not to `{ prop1: Wrapper<"hello"> }`. A bad error message results: `Type '{ prop1: Wrapper<"hello">; }' is not assignable to type '{ prop1: Wrapper<"hello">; }'. Two different types with this name exist, but they are unrelated.` (TS2719).
- It has a real effect on declaration emit. `repro/declaration_emit.ts` emits `export declare const r: { prop1: Wrapper<"hello">; }` here and on 5.7.2, versus `{ prop1: "hello"; }` on 5.6.3.
- Likely area: how `typeToString` and `typeToTypeNode` print the mapped type for this inferred `T`, since the inline assertion changes only how the type is printed. I did not confirm the cause.

**Artifacts:** `repro/repro.ts` (report code), `repro/repro_separate_line.ts` (control), `repro/run.js`, `repro/declaration_emit.ts`, all in /work/runs/d0df9187ff/repo. No production code was changed.
